fields.title: Debt as a Loan Interest
fields.keyTakeaway: Debt is measured by overpayment on specific items in the plan, and debt in an area that is not developing does not need to be paid off.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The team asks for a quarter for refactoring. How to understand if it is worth it, and how to explain this to management?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: The conversation about technical debt is usually held in the language of quality and ends in nothing or a concession without understanding. Both sides are unhappy, and the decision is made based on volume. Translating it into money makes the conversation short.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: The debt metaphor is accurate in one place: **debt has an [[interest-on-debt|interest rate]] that is paid constantly.**
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: *Overpayment on tasks.* Every feature in the affected area costs more. Measured by comparing estimates of similar tasks in different parts of the system. *Incidents.* Debt generates failures. Measured by time spent on incidents in this area. *Slowdown of hiring and onboarding.* New people take longer to get up to speed. *Rejection of opportunities.* Features that are not built because they are expensive. The largest and most invisible item.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/items/0: Take 4–6 plan items for the next two quarters.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/items/1: Estimate each as-is and as-it-would-be without debt.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/items/3: Compare with the cost of remediation.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: Formulation for management: **not "the schema is bad", but "these five features cost 14 weeks instead of 6, and the gap will remain in the next quarter".**
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: Separately — **not every debt is worth paying off.** Debt in an area that is not developing brings no interest. The criterion is the intersection of debt with the plan.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: An example from the catalog domain, analyzed in `DS3-N2-L2`, recalculated for the conversation with management.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Overpayment is 13 weeks. Remediation is 6 weeks. Plus incidents: over half a year, 3 out of 12 were related to this area.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: The decision was made in a single meeting. The key was that all four items were already in the approved plan — meaning the overpayment was not hypothetical, but agreed upon.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Reverse example: the team suggested rewriting the notification service. Checking against the plan showed zero items in this area for two quarters. Postponed — debt brings no interest.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Estimates of "how it would be without debt" are approximate and prone to optimism. It is sensible to budget a margin and not base decisions on a 10–20% difference.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Debt is measured by overpayment on specific items in the plan, and debt in an area that is not developing does not need to be paid off.
